title: The Hundredth Piece
logline: In a hill-country kitchen before the New Year, a sweet-maker's hands move without looking, and a child's whole day depends on the first bite.
human_question: Can the same taste mean everything to one person and nothing much to another, in the same room?

premise.story: A family or small kitchen making traditional New Year sweets over several days: the maker's flat, practised rhythm after hundreds of pieces, an elder's careful tasting and judgement, and children waiting for the first batch to cool enough to eat.
premise.place: A home kitchen in a hill-country village in the weeks before the New Year.
premise.experience: Oil, sugar and pattern; the contrast between a tired, expert hand and a child's undivided delight.

concept_links.why: This is close to the concept's own story seed: the same sweet bringing delight to one person and a neutral, practised routine to another, which is feeling following the object and the person rather than the object alone [C032-P:L43]. The idea that pleasant feeling is 'where wanting begins' is the group's own editorial framing, not a claim stated in this digest's extracts, and the film should not present it as source teaching.
The sweets themselves are a small, ordinary example of the sense-sphere world: taste, smell and sight together, wanted keenly by some and handled with flat skill by others [C004-P:L25].

what_camera_could_observe: The maker's rhythm after many repetitions
An elder tasting and judging a batch
Children waiting, then eating the first cooled piece
Sweets packed for visitors and the New Year table
what_must_be_real: The family's actual New Year preparations and their own account of who taught whom. Nothing staged beyond normal cooking.

possible_arc.opening: The first batter poured into hot oil before dawn.
possible_arc.turn: A child can't wait for the sweets to cool.
possible_arc.ending_open: The sweets are finished, shared, or run out before the visitors arrive. Reality decides.

requirements: A family actively making traditional sweets for the New Year
Consent to film children in a home setting, from parents or guardians
A kitchen with room for close, unobtrusive filming

suggestions.name: A village home kitchen near Badulla
suggestions.why: A hill-country district with strong village New Year traditions.
suggestions.verify: No family has been contacted; this is a plausible setting, not a confirmed location.

risks: Nostalgic, touristic imagery without a real family story underneath
Filming children requires full guardian consent throughout
drop_if: No family will allow filming across the full preparation, or will not consent to filming children

connections.note: Both are about giving something to eat, and whose pleasure the giving is really for.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
